subject: Hosting scope decomposition + SOC 2 artifacts & VPC operator appendix
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@medisys.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medisys.com
Date: 2026-03-03T08:11:00Z
Subject: Clarify hosting scope + requested SOC2/CAIQ artifacts

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the time today. As we scope our pilot for EU-only deployment we need a concise decomposition of what components of Redwood's service will be running in-region vs global control plane. Specifically Medisys security is asking for: 

- A short diagram / bulleted decomposition that shows: API control plane, inference runtime, keystore/KMS flow, telemetry/metrics aggregation, and any cross-region egress paths.
- A redacted SOC 2 Type II report or summary that covers infrastructure boundaries.
- A CAIQ crosswalk showing how Redwood maps CAIQ answers to our control objectives (we can start with a simple spreadsheet).
- The VPC operator contact list and on-call escalation steps for private deployments (we'll need operator names and phone/email).

Can you provide these artifacts, or point me to a secure drive where procurement/security can pull them? We are trying to keep the data residency commitment strictly EU (no inference tokens leaving region), but we also need clarity on telemetry aggregation and KMS key flow.

Goal: receive artifacts and a short (1-page) narrative we can share with Medisys InfoSec by Friday 2026-03-05.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Turner

Hannah / Jordan —

I've prepared an initial bundle and marked items that require redaction or legal gating. Summary of what I'm attaching: 

1) SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2025_redacted.pdf (redacted sections: customer-specific contract excerpts & explicit internal IP addresses). This is a vendor-facing redaction; full unredacted report requires IGA approval.

2) CAIQ_crosswalk_Medisys.xlsx — this maps CAIQ control IDs to our internal policy artifacts and includes a short note where we rely on cloud-provider responsibility (e.g., physical data center controls). 

3) VPC_operator_contacts_redwood.csv — includes operator name, role, email, pager, and region. Note: for EU private deployments the primary operator is Tomasz Kowalski (on-call) with secondary Jordan Blake for escalation.

4) keystore_segmentation_overview.png — a simplified flow showing customer-owned KMS key binding, in-region keystore, and optional HSM tie-in for on-prem/private deployments.

Caveats / items for Medisys review: 
- Telemetry: aggregated anonymized metrics (latency/cost) are sent to our control plane for ops; we can provide a filtered export that excludes PII and request-level identifiers. If the requirement is zero-control-plane telemetry leaving the EU, we need to plan an isolated control plane deployment (supported on Private) — that is a separate on-prem/VPC deploy workstream.
- KMS: by default, customer-managed keys can be used (we support KMS key partitioning by tenant and per-region keys). The diagram shows how an AES-wrapped key material flows; for HSM attestations, procurement needs to sign the HSM addendum.

I uploaded the bundle to the Medisys folder and added ACLs for alice.turner@medisys.com and security@medisys.com. Links below. I can redact further if legal asks.

Hi Alice / Medisys security team —

Thanks for the patience. Per your Friday deadline we've uploaded a compact artifact bundle and a one-page narrative that calls out region-hosting commitments for EU-only pilots. High level: 

- Inference runtime: deployed in EU region nodes (in-region GPU pools). Customer data and token processing remains in-region.
- Control plane: metadata and orchestration are handled by the Redwood control plane by default (hosted), which operates globally. For customers requiring EU-only telemetry/control-plane isolation we offer Redwood Private (VPC) with a local control plane.
- KMS/keys: customer-managed keys are supported. Keystore segmentation ensures per-tenant key partitions; HSM integration is available for Private installs and requires the HSM addendum.
- Telemetry: by default we aggregate anonymized metrics to a global analytics cluster. We have provided an export option and described the isolated control plane path in the narrative.

What we uploaded (Drive link and attached to DocuSign where required):
- 1-page narrative: hosting_scope_decomposition_1pager.pdf
- SOC 2 type II (redacted): SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2025_redacted.pdf
- CAIQ crosswalk: CAIQ_crosswalk_Medisys.xlsx
- VPC operator contacts: VPC_operator_contacts_redwood.csv
- Keystore flow: keystore_segmentation_overview.png

Access: the Drive folder is shared with alice.turner@medisys.com and security@medisys.com. If you prefer SSO-based access or an SFTP transfer for legal archives, tell us which and we'll provide the link.

Next steps suggested: 
1) Medisys security confirms whether the global control plane is acceptable for pilot analytics. If not, we will trigger the Private/isolated control-plane workstream and provide a timeline and statement of work (SOW).
2) If HSM-backed keys are required, procurement signs the HSM addendum; we can include the keystore HSM runbook.

If you'd like I can schedule a 30-minute run-through next week with Irene and Jordan to walk the diagram and the CAIQ crosswalk.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
